chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked him about hunted game: a man strikes it with a sword, pierces it with his spear, or shoots it with his arrow and kills it, having mentioned the name of Allah at the time he did that. He said:
"Eat it, for there is no problem with it."

key_terms.بِالسَّيْفِ: with the sword as a hunting weapon
key_terms.سَمَّى: he mentioned the name of Allah
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm or objection in it

ai.seo_question: Is hunted game lawful to eat if it is killed by a sword, spear, or arrow after mentioning the name of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning hunted game killed by a weapon such as a sword, spear, or arrow. If the hunter mentioned the name of Allah at the time of the act, then eating the prey is permitted and there is no objection to it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4130 - Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi asked Imam (as) about hunting when a man strikes the prey with his sword, pierces it with his spear, or shoots it with his arrow, and he had mentioned the name of Allah (swt) (Bismillah) at the time of doing so.
Imam (as) said: "Eat it, and there is no problem with it."
